opinions.title: CR BEVERAGE (2460.HK)：Dividend payout, share buyback, and increased holdings by major shareholders boost confidence, while a fundamental inflection point is approaching
opinions.opi_all: {"description":"Key takeaway The company’s dividend payout, share buyback, and management shareholding increase boosted confidence in the short term. The company also improved operational and management performance through channel structure adjustments, regional organizational restructuring, headquarters streamlining, optimized business incentive mechanisms, and accelerated digitalization. It is actively implementing reforms in channels and products, with expectations for a medium- to long-term business recovery. The company’s self‑owned production capacity is gradually coming online, which will drive a gradual increase in gross margin. The penetration of medium and large-sized packaged water is steadily rising, complemented by rapid growth in the company's beverage segment. Leveraging existing distribution channels and teams, economies of scale are increasingly taking effect, likely optimizing the company’s expense ratio. Flagship beverages like Zhiben Qingrun (chrysanthemum tea) have the potential to open further growth avenues, positioning the company to evolve into a platform-based beverage company. Event Company announces dividend payout plan The company announced that, following board approval and in order to enhance shareholder returns, it expects to declare annual dividends to shareholders for each fiscal year from 2026 to 2028 of no less than RMB0.37 per share, including interim, final, and special dividends, and will determine more favorable distribution plans based on earnings growth. The plan focuses on “long-term and sustainable development” as well as shareholder return requirements and expectations, aiming to establish a continuous and stable return mechanism. Quick Take Packaged water remained under pressure amid business adjustments; awaiting a turning point in recovery By product, in 2025 the company’s packaged water/beverages recorded revenue of RMB9.504bn/RMB1.499bn, YoY -21.6%/+7.3% respectively. Among which, 2H growth rates were -19.7%/-10.9% respectively. By sub‑category, revenue from small‑size packaged water/medium‑to‑large packaged water/barreled water was RMB5.4bn/RMB3.6bn/RMB0.5bn, YoY -23%/-21%/-4% respectively. The wider decline in full‑year packaged water revenue was mainly due to intensified industry competition, leading players capturing market share, and the company’s ongoing channel adjustments, which reduced packaged water sales volume. At the same time, due to the strong substitution effect of barreled water, demand for small‑size bottled water declined, leading to a notable revenue drop. In 2025, the beverage business launched 23 new SKUs, meeting differentiated consumer needs across on‑the‑go, sharing, and home consumption scenarios, and building a second growth curve. Growth of beverage products slowed in 2H, likely related to the pace of new product launches and channel inventory clearance. The company will adhere to its nationwide expansion strategy, continue to expand channels such as catering, and launch new beverage products, which may open up new growth opportunities. In 1H26, the company advanced organizational transformation, reforms to incentive mechanisms, and digitalization initiatives. It enhanced regional authority, enabling decisions to better align with the market and respond more flexibly to competition, while streamlining channel layers and clearing channel inventory. In the short term, due to increased rainfall weather since May, attention should be paid to channel recovery. Structural adjustment: Profitability under pressure On the profit side, the company’s gross margin in 2025 was 45.7%, YoY -1.6pct. Gross margin in 2H was 44.4%, YoY -0.4pcts. The decline narrowed compared with 1H, mainly due to changes in product mix, continued increases in discount intensity, and lower capacity utilization. The selling expense ratio in 2025 was 34.3%, YoY +4.3pcts.
